newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN DLR VULNERABLE AFTER HITTING TWO YR LOW.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN DLR VULNERABLE AFTER HITTING TWO YR LOW.

text.p: The Australian dollar was looking vulnerable to fall further after failing to move convincingly away from its overnight two year low during trading on Friday.

After initially rallying to near US$0.74 in London, the dollar dropped over one cent to US$0.7295, its lowest level since July 1995, in New York trade on Thursday and failed to bounce significantly from that level in local trade.

By 5.00 p.m. (0700 GMT) the Australian dollar was trading at US$0.7311/16, its lowest local trading close since the middle of July 1995. While slightly up on its early US$0.7304/09, it was still almost half a cent under Thursday's US$0.7355/60 close.
"It's up a little bit, but the Aussie's looking shaky," one trader said of the dollar's performance on the day.
The market seemed to share a similar view, with traders reporting a lack of solid buying and a market wary of potential sellers in a thin New York market ahead of the weekend.
"We haven't heard of anyone today that has been thinking about about squaring up," the trader said.
Uncertainty about the direction of interest rates remains a weight on the Australian dollar, and will remain so as long as a sixth interest rate cut is seen as a possibility.
As a result, traders said the dollar will find it difficult to maintain a rally, and will have a pronounced downside bias.
"I think the next seven days, we'll see the Aussie under some terrific pressure, but I think it's going to be a slow grind down from here," the trader said.
However, just as there were plenty of sellers into rallies, a freefall towards US$0.72 and lower was not expected.
"It's still got a target of US$0.7250, but I wouldn't try and sell in US$0.7250," he said, explaining that although US$0.7170 was a longer term target, the dollar would pause in its decline.
The dollar matched its performance against the U.S. on the crosses, falling heavily overnight and failing to substantially rebound during local trading.

Against the yen, the dollar ended at 86.51/61, almost level with an opening 86.53/63 and well down on Thursday's local close of 87.20/30. On the trade weighted index it held steady at 57.6 through the day after having closed at 58.0 on Thursday.
There is little data of interest next week apart from a speech by Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane on Tuesday, meaning the pressure will remain on the dollar in the near term.

Macfarlane will talk on the topic of monetary policy and growth in his first appearance since the July 30 rate cut and the early July announcement that the RBA had sold two thirds of its gold reserves earlier this year.
